Commentary.Commentary: We are back for the chase! Indian players are seen in the huddle and they disperse now to take their respective positions. Shai Hope and Brandon King are the openers for West Indies. Windies need a solid start from them. Deepak Chahar to start with the ball for India with two slips in place. Here we go...
...THE RUN CHASE…

Right then, India have posted a good score here and a Windies batters need to step up their game to chase this total down. They have failed to cross 200 in this series so far and it would not be an easy task even today. Can they grab 10 important World Cup Super League points? An interesting second-half of this game coming up.

Shreyas Iyer is down for the chat. He says that it wasn't easy to bat early on as the ball was seaming and swinging and him and Shikhar decided just to take it slow. He adds that the bowlers were also not sticking to one line or length and it was a test of patience as batting did get easy later on. He mentions that the wicket was a bit two-paced and the opposition came out with a good bowling plan. He mentions that the score they have is a really good one on this surface but it might get easier for batting later on and they will have to bowl well to get the win. Also says that he is ready to bowl if the captain needs him and is disappointed at himself for getting out the way he did especially with 15 odd overs still left.

West Indies with their fragile batting lineup needed to take early wickets to restrict India to a chaseable score and they did just that, Alzarri Joseph getting rid of Sharma and Kohli in the same over yet again. Odean Smith with all his x-factor managed to get the wicket of struggling Dhawan in his first over. West Indies were denied wickets in the middle overs after that as the partnership build but Walsh provided the important breakthrough just when the game seems to be drifting away and then came back to take the wicket of another set batter Iyer in the 38th over. They would have been hoping to restrict India to a lesser total after that but now have a decent score to chase on this pitch and need to bat better than what they have done so far.

When you talk about India playing an ODI game more often than not you will see top 3 or one of the top 3 playing a major role with the bat. However, it was not the case today as all three of them departed early. It was down to the rising stars of Indian cricket, Iyer and Pant to rebuild the innings. They did their job to perfection and stitched together a partnership of 110 runs. Both of them went on to get to their respective fifties on the way but Pant could not carry on and fell in the 30th over. SKY could not hold on for long and Iyer also departed while trying to up the ante against the spinners. It was Deepak Chahar who seems to be on a mission to prove himself as an all-rounder, provided the impetus at the end of the innings and Sundar also played a handy knock in the end. Overall India will be pleased with their effort with the bat.

India have gone past 260 here and they will be happy with this total after losing three early wickets. West Indies bowled well in the patches but with little more discipline they might have restricted India under 250 here. There is help for the bowlers in this pitch and India will fancy their chances of defending this total.

OUT! Cleaned up! Jason Holder gets his fourth and India have been bundled out on the final delivery of the innings. A slower length ball, angling into leg stump. Mohammed Siraj tries to repeat the trick as he shuffles across and looks to scoop it over short fine leg. Siraj though is undone by the lack of pace and misses the ball completely. The ball crashes into leg stump. India end with 265/10!

FOUR! Where did that come from? A yorker, on middle. Mohammed Siraj anticipates the line of the ball. He then paddles it past short fine leg and picks up a boundary. well and shuffles across to get insi
Prasidh Krishna is the last man in.

OUT! CAUGHT! Jason Holder has his third wicket and what a brilliant spell at the death it has been from him! A high full toss, on off. Washington Sundar looks to lift it over mid off but it's a bit too high to get a decent connection, Sundar only manages to slicee it hogh and towards the mid off region. Odean Smith strolls towards it from extra cover and takes a simple catch. An important knock from Sundar comes to an end.
Commentary.Howout: c Odean Smith b Jason Holder

Commentary.Commentary: Angled into middle and leg. This is driven down to long on for no run.
FOUR! Slower one, banged into the deck. Sundar pulls it hard and behind the man at the square leg fence for a boundary.
Holder with a perfect yorker, angling onto middle. Sundar just about manages to keep it out.
Jason Holder to bowl the last over.
On a good length, outside off. Mohammed Siraj goes for a big heave but is nowhere close to making a connection on that one.
A good length ball, around 141 kph and on off. Siraj backs away looking to cut but misses.
Full, on leg. This is drilled down to long on for a run.
SIX! Right off the screws this time! A length ball, on leg stump. Washington Sundar lifts it high and the ball sails over the wide long on fence for a biggie.
Swing and a miss! Back of a length again, in excess of 140 kph and over middle. Sundar looks to thump it over long on but doesn't make a connection.
Back of a length, around leg. Washington Sundar backs away and looks to heave it over the mid-wicket fence. He mistimes it badly and the ball falls around the mid-wicket region. No run taken.
Shorter in length, down the leg side. Siraj flicks it down to fine leg but Sundar isn't interested in a single as it is the last delivery of the over.
Very full, on off. Siraj pushes it out to cover.
Mohammed Siraj is the next man in.

OUT! TAKEN! Sensational catch behind the stumps by Shai Hope! Jason Holder hurls across a short ball from 'round the stumps and angles it around the helmet. Kuldeep Yadav looks to hook it away but gets a glove on it. Hope with an athletic effort, jumping high and to his right, pouches it with one hand and Holder picks up his second wicket. The Windies pulling things back a bit in the final overs.
Commentary.Howout: c Shai Hope b Jason Holder

Commentary.Commentary: This is banged in short, on the body. Sundar pulls it down to deep backward square leg for a run. The 250 is up for India.
Slower delivery, pitched up and on off. Yadav stylishly works it through the point region for one more.
A yorker, on off. Sundar jams it out to third man for a single.
Back of a length, angled across off. Yadav hops and dabs it down to short third man.
WIDE! Another wayward delivery from Odean Smith. Short and wide, a bit too wide for the umpire's liking.
Slower again, on off. This is stroked towards cover for a single.
A slower full toss, dipping on the batter. Sundar eases it towards point.
Short this time, on leg. Yadav pulls it in front of square for a single.
Sloppy bit of fielding. Back of a length, around off. Yadav steers it to the left of the fielder at third man. Bravo misfields and allows the batters to come back for the second.
Around the top of off. Yadav looks to work it on the leg side but gets beaten on the inside edge.
WIDE! This is pushed well wide of the off stump. Wide signalled.
Through! Short and a bit wide. Kuldeep Yadav cuts it late and the ball flies through the man at third slip and towards third man. They get a single.
A length ball, angling across off. Left alone by Yadav.
Kuldeep Yadav is the next man in.

OUT! CAUGHT BEHIND! Nice piece of bowling from Jason Holder and Deepak Chahar departs after a brisk knock. Chahar makes room leg side and looks to advanace. Holder follows hism with an off-cutter, bowled into the pitch. Chahar is way too early into the pull and the ball comes off the toe end of the bat and balloons up towards the keeper. Shai Hope takes the simplest of catches and Holder has his man.
Commentary.Howout: c Shai Hope b Jason Holder

Commentary.Commentary: Easy two! Chahar moves leg side and Holder follows him with a slower delivery, at the body. Chahar tucks it away through mid-wicket for a couple.
Very full, on off. Sundar works it towards the vacant mid-wicket region for a run.
Full, on off. This is stroked through mid off for a single. The fifty partnership also comes up between Chahar and Sundar.
WIDE! A slower bumper, outside off. Chahar leaves it in the hopes of it being a bit too high and does get the call in the end. Wided.
Jason Holder (5-1-17-0) comes on to replace Hayden Walsh.

A single to end the over! Alzarri Joseph goes short again on off. Deepak Chahar looks to pull but the ball catches the faint edge of his blade and hits his shoulders. It goes towards third man for a single.
FOUR! A lucky boundary this time! A length delivery on off. Chahar looks to defend it but the ball catches the outside edge of his blade. It races away towards the third man fence for a boundary.
Shorter this time, outside off at 140.6 kph. Chahar swings across the line but misses.
Slightly back of a length, around leg. Sundar works it past square leg for a single.
On a length, on middle. Chahar works it to fine leg for a single.
Shorter and around leg. Sundar pulls it to fine leg for a single.
Quicker and slightly shorter outside off. Chahar looks to cut but misses this time.  Deepak Chahar ruins Walsh's spell a little but still a good comeback by Walsh.
SIX! This time a biggie! Deepak Chahar is taking on Walsh here! A tossed up delivery on off. Chahar gets under it and slogs it over long on sailing into the stands.
FOUR! Short and punished! Walsh this time bowls it short outside off. Chahar cuts it over point for a boundary.
FOUR! Brilliant from Chahar! A tossed up deliveryb on off. Chahar slams it straight down the ground for a boundary. No chance for the fielder in the deep.
Flatter and around off. Chahar steers it to third man.
Tossed up on off. Chahar blocks it out.
A fuller delivery, outside off. Chahar steers it to deep point for a single.
Back of a length, on middle. Chahar works it to mid-wicket now.
Shorter length on off. Chahar rides the bounce and blocks it.
On a length, on middle. Sundar works it to deep square leg for a single.
Back of a length, on off. Sundar blocks it out.
FOUR! Sundar starts the over with a boundary! Short and around off. Sundar upper cuts it fine towards third man for a boundary.
Alzarri Joseph (7-1-33-2) is back into the attack.
Quicker and shorter. Chahar punches it off the back foot but can't get it through the inner ring on the off side.
FOUR! Tossed up, around off. Deepak Chahar presses forward and drives it exquisitely through the cover region to collect a boundary.
Dragged down, around leg. Washington Sundar pulls it behind square on the leg side for one more.
Tossed up, around off. This is driven through extra cover for a single.
Well bowled! Walsh yorks Chahar with a very full delivery on middle. Chahar manages to keep it out.
This is sliding across off. Sundar guides it past backward point for a single.
Shorter and flatter around off. Chahar chops it to backward point.
Shorter and flatter around off. Chahar steers it to point.
A flatter delivery on middle. Chahar works it to mid-wicket.
SIX! 200 up for India! A tossed up delivery on off. Chahar dances down the track and hammers it straight down the ground for a maximum.
On a length, around off. Chahar blocks it out.
A flatter delivery on middle. Sundar works it to deep mid-wicket for a single.
The umpire signals for Powerplay 3! The fielding side can now have up to 5 fielders outside the 30-yard circle until the end of the innings.
Nicely bowled! A flighted delivery drifted into off. The ball just holds its line and zips past the outside edge of Chahar's bat.
Short and wide again, turning away a bit. Chahar misses the cut again and lets out a sigh of disappointment.
Nicely drifted into middle. Deepak Chahar stays solid in defense.
A googly now, on middle. Chahar works it towards mid-wicket.
Short and wide, Deepak Chahar gets beaten past the outside edge as he looks to cut.
On a length, around leg. Sundar turns it through square leg for a run.
Tossed up, on off. Chahar prods and bunts it out towards cover, looking for the single but Sundar sends him back.
On off. Kept out on the off side.
Flatter one, around off. Chahar works it through the cover region and picks up a couple.
This is a bit shorter and wider. Chahar makes room and looks to cut but mistimes it towards mid on.
Flighted, around off. Sundar presses forward and drives it down to long off for a run.
On the pads. This is pushed towards mid on.
On middle, Sundar pushes it down to long on for a single.
A tad bit short, around off. Deepak Chahar plays it off the back foot through covers and picks up a run.
On middle. Defended out.
On a length, quicker and turning away sharply. Chahar is beaten all ends up.
Here comes the googly! Turning in sharply from middle stump. Chahar doesn't pick it up and gets rapped on the pads.
Deepak Chahar walks out at number 8.

OUT! CAUGHT! Straight to the man and this is a huge wicket for Hayden Walsh and West Indies. Nicely tossed up, around off. Iyer makes a bit of room leg side and looks to go inside-out, over the long off fence. Iyer doesn't get anywhere near the pitch of the ball and ends up lifting it straight towards the man at the long off fence. Darren Bravo takes a comfortable catch and Walsh has his second wicket. Shreyas Iyer departs after a well-made 80 and he will be disappointed. Can the Windies clean up the Indian tail now?
Commentary.Howout: c Darren Bravo b Hayden Walsh

Commentary.Commentary: On a length, around off. Iyer opens the face of the bat and plays it through point for one more.
Tossed up, on middle. Sundar eases it down to long on for a single.
Around middle and leg, this is worked through square leg for a run.
On off. Kept out on the off side.
FOUR! Short and wide, it is there to be hit and Shreyas Iyer doesn't miss out. Iyer rocks back and thumps it well in front of sweeper cover for a boundary.
Down the leg side, Sundar paddles it towards short fine leg for a single.
Sliding across off, Sundar eases it through backward point for one more.
Short and wide. This is cut away to deep point for a single.
On a length, Iyer tries to punch off the back foot but can't get it through.
Early call for two and they get it with ease. Full, on middle and leg. Iyer works it towards wide long on for two.
A touch shorter, around off and this one bounces a bit extra. Iyer looks to cut but is undone by the extra bounce.

Dragged down, around leg. Shreyas Iyer looks to go a bit too hard at it and is way too early in his pull shot. The ball comes off the gloves and goes to the opposite side of the keeper as he looked to collect it down the leg side. Lucky!
Hayden Walsh (5-0-31-1) is back into the attack.
Flatter, around off. Washington Sundar hangs back and cuts it late and fine, past the fielder at short third man. Odean Smith gives the chase and does really well to keep it down to a couple.
Shreyas Iyer seems to be suffering from cramps. The heat of Ahmedabad can do that to you. He is having some energy drinks and is ready to resume now.
On off, this is driven through mid off for a single.
Flatter, on off. Iyer backs away but can't get it through the cover region.
A touch short and wide. Iyer rocks back and cuts it in front of square on the off side for a couple.
Drifted into middle and leg. This is pushed towards mid on.
Slower through the air, on off. Iyer watchfully keeps it out on the off side.
A good-length ball, around off. Sundar taps it onto the off side.
A length ball, outside off. Sundar leaves it alone.
Back of a length, around off. Iyer steers it down to third man for a run.

FOUR! Shreyas Iyer tries to toy with the bowler and manages to come out on top. Iyer shuffles a bit inside the crease and Smith fires it in at the legs. Iyer manages to heave it through mid-wicket and collects a boundary.
WIDE! Way too short, outside off. Iyer leaves it alone and a wide is called.

Excellent bumper! Smith with a well-directed bouncer around the throat of Shreyas Iyer. Iyer is completely taken by surprise and manages to get a glove on it. The ball pops up and lands safely back onto the deck.
Short and a bit wide. Iyer thinks about having a poke at it but decides against it in the end.
This is angled into middle. Sundar flicks it towards mid-wicket.
Flatter delivery, on off. Sundar gets behind the line of the ball to block.
Quicker and fuller, outside off. This is sliced away to point.
Washington Sundar is the next man in.

OUT! TAKEN! A really sharp catch taken by Shamarh Brooks and Suryakumar Yadav is sent packing really early. This is pushed through, on off. SKY gets to the pitch of the ball and looks to force it over extra cover. The ball comes off the splice of the bat and flies low towards cover-point. Brooks over there reacts quickly and takes a brilliant low catch down to his right. Fabian Allen has the breakthrough and the Windies crawling back into the contest.
Commentary.Howout: c Shamarh Brooks b Fabian Allen

Commentary.Commentary: FOUR! Tossed up, around off. Suryakumar Yadav gets inside the line of the ball to sweep it fine and gets a top edge. Luckily for him, the ball flies behind square and into the vacant backward square leg fence.
Excellent running! Slowed up, on off. Iyer plays it with soft hands towards cover and sets off for a quick single.
Shorter one, angled into middle. Yadav sways away and looks to ramp it over the keeper but it's a bit too close for comfort.
A yorker, on off. Yadav manages to jam it out.
Back of a length, close to the off pole. Iyer hops back and dabs it towards to short third man for one.
A length ball, outside off. Iyer looks to thrash it through point but doesn't connect.
Back of a length, on the body. Yadav flicks it behind square on the leg side for a single.
Just short! Short and wide, SKY looks to open the face of the bat and get it behind point but gets it off the leading edge towards extra cover.
WIDE! Odean Smith has been wayward throughout this match. Sliding down leg and a wide is calle.d
Good-length delivery, on off. Iyer blocks it out.
Back of a length, nipping back in off the surface. Iyer is late on it as he looks to guide it behind for a single. He gets caught on the crease and gets hit on the gloves.
On the pads, Yadav looks to flick but misses. The ball goes off his pads to the left of the keeper.
WIDE! Way too short and the ball flies over the keeper's head. Back-to-back wides.
WIDE! This is spilled down the leg side. Wided.
Length again, outside off. Left alone by Yadav.
Uppish...but safe! On a good length, at the hips. Yadav clips it through the square leg region for a run.
Back of a length, angled into off. Iyer hangs back and dabs it down to backward point for a quick single.

DRINKS! Hayden Walsh has just broken a 110-run stand between Shreyas Iyer and Rishabh Pant who were taking the game away from the Windies. After a strong start with the ball from the visitors, India have managed to claw their way back into the match with half-centuries from Iyer and Pant. With still 20 overs to go, the first innings is set up nicely. A couple of wickets in the next 5 or so overs and the Windies will be able to regain the lost advantage. India need another decent stand here. Suryakumar Yadav comes in at number 6.

OUT! CAUGHT BEHIND! Pant departs after looking so good. He is gutted and punches his bat with his hands. A wicket against the run of play for West Indies. Walsh bowls this quicker and slightly shorter around off. Maybe not enough short for Pant to cut. He, however, goes for the cut shot and ends up getting a faint edge of his blade to keeper. Shai Hope takes a fine catch and this partnership that was threatening to take the game away is broken now.
Commentary.Howout: c Shai Hope b Hayden Walsh

Commentary.Commentary: FOUR! Easy pickings for Pant! The ball is turning in from middle. Pant heaves it towards deep mid-wicket for a boundary.
On middle this time. Pant works it to mid-wicket.
Slower in the air on off. Iyer pushes it down the ground for a single.
Pant brings out a sweep shot now! A fuller delivery on middle. Pant sweeps it to fine leg for a single.
Tossed up, around off. Pant rocks back and tries to cut but misses.
Hayden Walsh (4-0-25-0) comes from the opposite end now.
On middle. Pant works it to deep square leg for a single.
Flatter on off. Pant leans forward and pushes it back to the bowler.
A fuller delivery on off. Iyer drives it to deep cover for a single.

Fifty for Pant off just 47 balls! He is showing lot of maturity now. A fuller delivery on middle. Pant skips down the track and works it to square leg for a single. He has looked comfortable right from the time he came onto bat.
Shorter length this time on off. Iyer pulls it to deep mid-wicket and the batters run just a single. That looked like a comfortable two.
Tossed up on off. Iyer gets forward and blocks it.
On a length, around off. Iyer steers it to third man for a single.

FOUR! Top-edge but a boundary for Iyer! Short delivery around off. Iyer looks to pull but gets a top edge. The ball goes towards fine leg and one bounce over the fence. The fielder at fine leg has no chance.
Short and bit of width this time. Iyer goes for the cut-shot but misses.
On a length, on off. Iyer blocks it out this time.
Ohh..just over mid on! A length ball, on off. Iyer looks to hit it over long on. He fails to get enough timing but the ball has enough to go over Bravo there for a couple.
WIDE! Shorter length delivery this time. Iyer first looks to pull it but then lets it go. Too high.
On a length, on off. Iyer blocks it out.
FOUR! Boundary to end the over and India are moving along nicely now. A fuller delivcery, around off. Pant leans forward and drives it right of long off for a boundary.
WIDE! This is down the leg side now. Pant looks to clip it but misses.
50 for Shreyas Iyer! Comes back from Covid and delivers for his team under  pressure. This is fuller on off. Iyer drives it to long off for a single.
Flatter around off. Iyer chops it to backward point.
Slower in the air on off. Urging Pant to go over the top. He resists and works it to deep mid-wicket for a single.
Nicely tossed up on middle. Iyer drives it towards long off for a single.
Tossed up on off. Pant works it to long on for a single.
Hayden Walsh to continue.
On a length, on middle at 134.5 kph. Iyer clips it to mid-wicket. 6 runs from the over.
Back of a length again, around leg. Iyer works it to fine leg for a couple.
Shorter length, around off. Iyer backs away and looks to cut but misses.

FOUR! Nicely played by Iyer! However it is the fumble in the deep that allows a boundary. A fuller delivery on middle. Iyer clips it through mid-wicket. Brandon King there dives as he runs to his left but fails to stop it.
Back of a length again, on off at 123.9 kph. Iyer blocks it out.
Back of a length, on middle. Iyer works it to mid-wicket.
FOUR! This boundary means that it is another good over for India! A shorter length delivery, outside off.Pushed quicker this time. Pant rocks back and cuts it past backward point for a boundary.
Flatter and shorter on off. Iyer rocks back and pushes this to long off for a single.
Tossed up, outside off. Pant drives it to deep cover for a single.
Tossed up on off. Iyer drives it off the inside half of his blade to long off for a single. Googly this time.
Slower in the air on off. Pant turns it to long on for a single.
Flatter delivery on middle. Pant works it to mid-wicket.
Shorter length delivery, outside off. Pant cuts it to third man for a single. 12 runs from the over.
FOUR! Ohh..just away from the fielder! A length delivery on off. Pant steps out towards the leg side and slams this past mid off for a boundary.
Excellent running! Back of a length, around middle. Pant works it towards backward square leg with soft hands and gets a couple.
On a length, around off. Iyer guides it past point this time for a single.
A length ball, on off. Iyer pushes it towards the off side and looks for a single but is sent back.
FOUR! Good shot, Iyer is growing in confidence now. A fuller delivery on off. Iyer lifts this over mid off with straight bat for a boundary.
A full toss on off. Iyer eases it down to long on for a single.
Quicker again on off. Iyer blocks it out.
A flatter delivery, outside off. Iyer chops it to backward point.
A quicker delivery on off at 91.3 kph. Pant cuts it to backward point for a single.
Flatter and shorter, outside off. Pant leaves it alone.
A fuller delivery on off. Pant drives it towards the off side. He gets an outside edge to short third man. A googly there.
On a length, on middle. Iyer blocks it out onto the truf this time. 3 runs from the first over of new spell by Roach.
Still something in the pitch. A good-length delivery, around off. Iyer looks to push at it but the ball beats him as it seams away sharply.
On a length, around off. Pant guides it to third man for a single.
This time an outside edge! A good-length delivery, on off. Iyer looks to work it towards the leg side. The ball straightens and catches the outside edge of his blade. A single towards the third man.
An inside-edge this time! A fuller delivery around off. Iyer looks to drive but gets the inside edge onto his pads.
Roach starts his new spell with a shorter length delivery, around off. Pant pulls it to fine leg for a single.
Kemar Roach (5-0-24-0) is back into the attack.
Slower in the air, on off. Iyer drives it towards the off side. Looks for a single but is sent back. 6 runs from the over without taking much risk.
Slightly quicker in air, outside off. Pant late-cuts it to short third man for a single. The fielder there does well to stop it with a dive.
Fuller on off. Iyer drives it to long off for a single.
Walsh overcompensates and bowls it shorter outside off. Iyer cuts it to deep point for a couple.
Fuller this time outside off. Iyer drives it to deep extra-cover and gets back for the second.
A flatter delivery on off to start. Iyer punches it back to the bowler.
Fuller again, around off. Pant looks for the cover drive but gets an inside edge back onto the pads.
Beaten! Holder pitches it fuller and tries to angle it away from around off. Pant strides out to defend but is beaten on the inside edge.
FOUR! Nicely done! Slower one, down the leg side. Rishabh Pant just gets a tickle on it and the ball goes very fine and into the fine leg fence.
Good running! Full and straight, this is pushed towards mid on and the batters are off for a quick single.
Length again, around off. Iyer taps it towards cover-point.

Well bowled and well played. A good length ball, around off. The ball bounces a bit extra and Pant does well to keep it along the ground. The ball goes off the handle of the bat down towards third man for a single.
Flatter one, sliding down leg. Pant flicks it behind square on the leg side for a quick single.
Dareted into the pads, Pant can't get it away and gets hit on the pads.
Pant advances and Allen drags back the length, outside off. Pant has to adjust and pushes it out on the leg side.
Very full, on off. Iyer manages to drive it past the diving bowler, down to long off for a single.
Quicker through the air, on off. Pant works it through mid-wicket for one.
The ball seems to be lost in the stands! This is another difficulty when you don't have spectators there. However, they have found it now and we are ready to resume.
SIX! All the way! Tossed up, around off. Rishabh Pant dances down the track and hits it with the spin and dispatches it well over the mid-wicket fence for a biggie.
Short this time, around middle and leg. Rishabh Pant makes a good connection and pulls it along the ground towards deep square leg. Single taken.
Good-length, wide of off and angling further away. Iyer just taps it through the backward point region for a run.
Pitched up, well outside off. Iyer doesn't play at it.
Short and wide, Pant hangs back and goes hard at the cut shot. He gets it past point but it'll only be a single.
On a good length, going across the off stump. Left alone by Pant.
Change of ends for Jason Holder. He replaces Odean Smith.
Back of a length, angling across the left-hander. Pant taps it towards cover-point.
Quicker and flatter, around off. Iyer defends it off the back foot.
This is fuller and wider and once again Iyer can't get it past point.
A touch short and wide, Iyer cuts it straight to point.
Flatter this time, on middle and there's a hint of turn there. Iyer keeps it out on the leg side.
Tossed up, on off. Pant heaves it towards deep mid-wicket for a single.
A flighted delivery, on off. Pant presses forward to defend.
Spin for the first time today. Fabian Allen is brought into the attack now.
A length ball, on off. Iyer blocks it out.
FOUR! Overpitched and punished! Full, on off. Iyer punches it right back past the bowler and picks up a boundary at the long on region.
Around off, this is pushed towards covers.

FOUR! 'Catch' is the cry but the ball goes a lot finer. This is a slower short ball, outside off. Shreyas Iyer has to check his shot and ends up ramping it towards the third man fence. Hayden Walsh over there doesn't quite pick it up and the ball goes one bounce over the fence.
Length this time, angling into middle and leg. Iyer keeps it out on the leg side.
Full, around off. This is driven straight towards mid off.
Odean Smith to continue. Nicholas Pooran would hope that the big man produces another wicket.
Short of a good length, on off. Iyer swivels and pulls it along the ground through mid-wicket for a run.
On off. Iyer defends it back onto the deck with soft hands.
This is bowled wider of off stump. Iyer watches it all the way through as he makes a leave.
Back of a length, around leg. Pant hangs back and jabs it down to deep mid-wicket for a single.
Pitched up, around off. Pant leaves it alone.
Around the top of off, Pant gets behind the line of the ball to make the block.
Length again, on the body. Iyer flicks it towards mid-wicket.
Back of a length, around off. Pant guides it behind point with hard hands and collects a single.
Smith switches to 'round the wicket now. He bowls a lovely length ball, in that channel around off. Pant is forced to have a poke at it but the ball whizzes past the outside edge.
Back of a length, on middle. Pant pulls it down to mid-wicket.
Smith bowls it a tad fuller, around off. Rishabh Pant looks to muscle it over the mid-wicket fence but one hand comes off the handle and the ball is skied beyond the mid on region. Two taken.
NO BALL! And now Smith oversteps! A length ball, outside off. Pant looks to cut but misses. Free-hit to follow.
WIDE! Too many wides at the moment from the Windies pacers. This is pushed full and well wide of off stump.

Drinks! India in a spot of bother here! They have lost their top 3 batters and it is upto the young middle-order now to bail them out of the trouble. West Indies bowlers came out with a plan and got some good help from the pitch and would be looking to get some more wickets in these middle-overs. Shreyas Iyer and Rishabh Pant are out there in the middle and a lot will depend on how long these two can stay together.
FOUR! A short ball, this is banged in around off. Rishabh Pant hops and manages to slap it well in front of square for a boundary.
Fuller one, around off. Iyer looks to work it leg side but mistimes it off the inner half of the bat onto the leg side.
FOUR! Nicely put away. A gentle half-volley, around middle and leg. Iyer clips it through the vacant mid-wicket region for a boundary.
Length again, outside off. Iyer leaves it alone.
A bit of yes and no in the middle. Back of a length, around off. Iyer taps it towards point and looks for a single but is sent back by Pant and rightly so.
Another tight single. A length ball, around off. Pant bunts it out on the off side and has to put in the dive to complete the run.
Living on the edge here Shreyas Iyer. On off, pushed gently towards cover for a risky single. No harm done though.
On a good length, around off. Iyer guides it down to third man for a single.
Back of a length, angling away from outside off. Iyer hangs back and looks to uppercut it but misses.

What was that all about! Back of a length, on middle. Iyer moves across in his crease and then backs away and goes for a wild swing across the line. He misses it and the ball goes over the stumps back to the keeper. Poor shot selection this by Shreyas Iyer.
Back of a length again at 138.2 kph on middle. Iyer works it to short mid-wicket.
Back of a length this time, around leg. Pant tucks it towards the leg side for a single.
On a length, outside off. Pant carefully lets it go.
A length ball, outside off. Left alone by Iyer. Jason Holder starts off with a maiden.
Peach! A length ball, close to off and just nipping in a bit. Shreyas Iyer is caught on the crease as the ball zips past the outside edge.

What was Shreyas Iyer doing there? A fullish ball, on off. Iyer nudges it towards mid-wicket and just sets off for a run. Rishabh Pant isn't interested and Darren Bravo has a shy at the batter's end. Bravo misses and Iyer is lucky to still be at the crease.
Good-length ball, outside off. Shreyas Iyer shoulders arms.
A hint of shape here for Holder. Fullish ball, around off and this one nips away a bit. Iyer does well to defend it out.
A length ball, angling in sharply from around off. Iyer looks to work it leg side but misses and gets rapped on the pads.
The umpire signals the start of Powerplay 2! The fielding side can now have as many as 4 fielders outside the 30-yard circle till the 40th over. Also, Jason Holder is now brought into the attack.
Back of a length, outside off. Pant watches it carefully and lets it go. Good start for Odean Smith.
Another one that bounces off sharply! An effort delivery this. Smith bangs this short around off. Pant just about manages to let it go as he takes his hands off the line of the ball.
Back of a length, on middle. Pant blocks it out.

OUT! CAUGHT! Shikhar Dhawan departs now and Odean Smith strikes in his first over! Short and wide outside off. It is there to hit for Shikhar Dhawan. He tries to cut it but again the extra pace and extra bounce produces an edge. The ball goes off the outside edge to first slip and Jason Holder there takes a good low catch. The big three at the top of the order are gone early for India and it is up to the middle-order now to show their potential.
Commentary.Howout: c Jason Holder b Odean Smith

Commentary.Commentary: Rishabh Pant walks in at number 5.
WIDE! This time a wide down the leg side! A shorter length delivery, around leg. Shikhar Dhawan looks to pull but misses.
Another delivery on that length, outside off. Shikhar Dhawan decides to let it go again.
Back of a length, outside off. Shikhar Dhawan leaves it alone.
WIDE! Smith starts with a wayward delivery! Back of a length, way outside off. Dhawan leaves it alone.
Here comes the first change in bowling. Odean Smith comes on to replace Alzarri Joseph.
Pulls his length back a little and serves this on off. Iyer is solid in his defence.
FOUR! Bread and butter for Shreyas Iyer! A fuller delivery, on middle and leg. Iyer is strong on his pads and clips it uppishly towards deep sqiuare leg for a boundary.
Nicely played! A length delivery on middle. Iyer clips it towards backward square leg for a couple.
A length delivery on middle at 133.8 kph. Shikhar Dhawan works it left of mid on for a single.
Shikhar Dhawan tries to use his feet again! A good-length delivery, outside off. Shikhar Dhawan skips down the track and then lets it go.
A good-length delivery, outside off. Seaming away a ittle. Shikhar Dhawan lets it go.
Back of a length, on off. Iyer rides the bounce and defends it solidly.
Superb delivery this time! A good-length delivery, around off at 137 kph. Iyer is rooted to his crease as he puts his bat to defend it but gets beaten as it seams away.
WIDE! Another short ball but this time it is too high. Iyer ducks under it.
WIDE! Shorter length delivery around leg this time. Iyer looks to pull it but misses. Therse is some excitement around the Windies players but the umpire calls it wide.
A fuller length delivery on middle this time. Iyer drives it back to the bowler.
On a length, on middle. Shikhar Dhawan works it past square leg for a single again.
Another quick single. Back of a length, on middle. Iyer drops it down towards the leg side and the batters steal a single.

Ohh..quick single this time! A length ball, on middle. Shikhar Dhawan works it to square leg and looks for a single. The fielder there picks it and has a shy at the batter's end but misses. Iyer puts in a dive and is safe.
Shorter length delivery on off. Shikhar Dhawan pulls it to fine leg for a single.
WIDE! This is seaming away and pitched way outside off. Shikhar Dhawan lets it go and the umpire call it wide.
On a length, outside off. Shikhar Dhawan advances a little and lets it go.
On a length, around off and nipping back in. Shikhar Dhawan looks to defend but the ball beats the inside edge of his blade.

SIX! 14 balls without a run and Shikhar Dhawan decides it is enough and smashes it for a maximum. A length delivery, outside off. Shikhar Dhawan skips down the track and hits it over covers for a maximum.
Back of a length, on off. Shikhar Dhawan goes back and blocks it.
On a length, on middle. Iyer defends it off the inner half of his blade past square leg for a single.
Short and wide outside off. Shikhar Dhawan tries to cut it but misses. 13 balls and he is yet to get off the mark.
On a length, on middle. The ball hurries Dhawan and hits him hig on the pads as he looks to defend.
Good pace and bounce this time! Back of a length, around off over 140 clicks. Shikhar Dhawan takes his bat away from the line of the ball and lets it go.
On a length, on middle at 137.6 kph on middle. Shikhar Dhawan blocks it back to the bowler.
A thick outside edge this time! A length ball, on off. Iyer drives it on up and gets the thick outside edge to third man for a single.
On a length, on middle at 139.3 kph. Iyer clips it to square leg.
Another leave by Dhawan. This is served on a length, outside off. A harmless delivery and Shikhar Dhawan lets it go.
A good-length delivery, outside off and slightly seaming away. Shikhar Dhawan leaves it alone.
On a length, around leg this time. Iyer clips it to fine leg for a single.
On a length, on off. Iyer defends it towards the point fielder this time.
A length ball, outside off. Iyer leaves it alone comfortably.
On a length, around off. Dhawan looks to defend but misses. The ball hits his back leg and there is an appeal. The umpire turns it down and the batters take a leg bye behind square on the off side.
A length delivery, outside off. Iyer lets it go. End of a double-wicket maiden by Alzarri Joseph. Brilliant stuff.
Shreyas Iyer is in early with India in a spot of bother.

OUT! CAUGHT BEHIND! Virat Kohli is gone now for a duck and it is another failure for the former skipper. This is a little unlucky though. A length delivery around leg. Kohli looks to clip it but gets a faint part of his blade and the ball goes left of Shai Hope. He gets across and takes an easy catch and two of the big wickets are gone now. West Indies are right on top now. Second time in this series that Alzarri Joseph has got Rohit and Virat in the same over, unreal!
Commentary.Howout: c Shai Hope b Alzarri Joseph

Commentary.Commentary: This is banged in short around 140 kph and outside off. Kohli shoulders arms and the ball just shoots up off the surface as the keeper collects around his face.
Virat Kohli is in at number 3.

OUT! CHOPPED ON! Rohit Sharma departs and Alzarri Joseph is the man with the first strike for the Windies. Back of a length, outside off. Sharma looks to drive it on up but gets the inside edge of his blade. The ball shatters the stumps and Rohit Sharma after looking so good in this innings has to walk back. A big strike for West Indies. Alzarri Joseph has bowled pretty good throughout this series.
On a length, on off at 136.8 kph. Sharma solidly blocks it towards the off side.
Sligthy short of a good-length this time. Sharma lets it go. Decent carry for the bowler.
Another ball and another leave! This is on a good-length, around off. Shikhar Dhawan watches it till the end and lets it go.
On a length, around off. A bit closer to the off pole this time. Shikhar Dhawan lets it go again.
Another one that seams away. However, it is starting way outside off and Shikhar Dhawan again leaves it comfortably.
This is wider again, outside off. Shikhar Dhawan carefully leaves it.
WIDE! Fuller and wider outside off. Shikhar Dhawan leaves it alone.
WIDE! A length ball, pushed wider. Shikhar Dhawan gives the charge and looks to go over extra cover but doesn't connect. Wide signalled.
A touch fuller, wide of off stump. Dhawan lets it through to the keeper.
This one nips in after passing the batter.A good-length delivery, outside off. Shikhar Dhawan leaves it as the ball nips in sharply.
Alzarri Joseph bangs this short on off. Rohit Sharma looks to pull but gets the inside edge onto his shoulders. Brisk start for India this. Rohit Sharma is looking in good touch.
A length ball, around off. Sharma defends it towards the backward point fielder this time.
Back of a length, on off. Sharma rides the bounce this time and blocks it.
FOUR! Another boundary for Sharma and he is up and running here. This is fuller on middle. Sharma clips it through mid-wicket for a boundary.
WIDE! This time Alzarri Joseph drifts down the leg side. Sharma looks to clip it but misses.
On a length, on off, Sharma defends it solidly this time.
FOUR! Nicely maneuvered! A short ball, outside off. Sharma fetches it and just roll his wrists to pull it behind square on the leg side for a boundary.
Alzarri Joseph to start with the other new ball.
A single to end the over! A fuller delivery on middle. Sharma pushes it to mid on for a single and reatin the strike.
On a length again, around off. Sharma gets back and blocks it.
A length ball, on off. Sharma blocks it out.

Nicholas Pooran has taken the DRS for an LBW decision. On the first replay, we can see that there is no bat involved and Ball Tracker then confirms that the ball was sliding well down leg. West Indies have wasted an early review here.

NOT OUT! A huge appeal for LBW but the umpire turns it down. A good-length delivery on off and nipping back in sharply this time. Sharma looks to defend but misses. He gets rapped up on the pads and there is a huge appeal. The umpire is unmoved and West Indies take a review. The replays roll in and  the Ultra Edge shows no bat involved. The Ball Tracker rolls and it shows that the ball is missing the stumps. So Rohit Sharma survives.
A good-length delivery this time, outside off. Sharma lets it go.
FOUR! Rohit Sharma starts off in style! Roach starts with a shorter length delivery, outside off. Sharma rocks back and cuts it past point for a boundary.

We are ready for play! West Indies are seen in a huddle as the Indian openers, Rohit Sharma and Shikhar Dhawan stride out to the middle. Kemar Roach to start proceedings with the ball here. West Indies take the knee as the Indian players are seen having a hand on the heart to show their support for the BLM movement. Let's play...

Nicholas Pooran says that they wanted to bowl first again and in the last match, they couldn't chase it down but will look to make amends today. Adds that the batters need to give themselves a chance by getting in and staying on the crease a bit longer. Informs that they have a forced change with Akeal Hosein missing out and Hayden Walsh coming in place of him.

Rohit Sharma says that they will bat first. He says that they always wanted to post some runs on the board and give the bowlers some chance to do what they did the other night. He adds that there was no dew in the last game and they want to post runs on the board and they want to give their bowlers another chance. He says that they have made three changes. KL has niggle and misses out. He adds that Hooda and Chahal also miss out today.

West Indies (Playing XI) - Shai Hope (WK), Brandon King, Darren Bravo, Shamarh Brooks, Nicholas Pooran (C), Jason Holder, Fabian Allen, Odean Smith, Hayden Walsh (In for Akeal Hosein), Alzarri Joseph and Kemar Roach.

India (Playing XI) - Rohit Sharma (C), Shikhar Dhawan (In for KL Rahul), Virat Kohli, Shreyas Iyer (In for Deepak Hooda), Rishabh Pant (WK), Suryakumar Yadav, Washington Sundar, Deepak Chahar (In for Shardul Thakur), Mohammed Siraj, Kuldeep Yadav (In for Yuzvendra Chahal) and Prasidh Krishna.
TOSS - Up goes the flip of the coin and Nicholas Pooran calls it. It lands in favor of India and Rohit Sharma has elected to BAT first.

PITCH REPORT - Deep Dasgupta is pitchside and he is joined by Ajit Agarkar. DDG says that there is a bit of breeze and it's exactly the same pitch as the last match. Ajit says that it is a lovely pitch and there was good bounce on offer for the faster bowlers but the same bounce might not be there as it looks more whitish. If the dew does come on, the sides might look to chase and DDG concludes by saying that it is a good ODI pitch with something in it for everyone.

The news going around is that we might see a couple of changes in the Indian side today. Kuldeep Yadav may get a look in. Meanwhile, Shikhar Dhawan is all set to be back at the top of the order. West Indies, on the other hand, might see their skipper, Kieron Pollard coming back.

West Indies, on the other hand, are facing similar problems they have faced in the past. Their batting group has failed to play out the allotted 50 overs and that hurt them in both the games so far. Shai Hope is the man they have been relying on in this format in recent times and it is high time that he delivers. The bowling has been pretty decent from the Windies and if their top-order can lay the foundation, they have the firepower to explode in the end. Can they lift their game and win this final ODI? Or will India continue to dominate? We shall find out. Toss and team sheets in a while.

India were expected to win this series despite a poor performance in South Africa and they have lived up to the expectations. However, the bigger goal for India is to try out some players in specific positions in specific conditions and with Deepak Hooda and Suryakumar Yadav putting up good performances in the middle order, India will be quite happy with how things have panned out. Another concern was that India was not taking wickets in the middle overs and India have rectified that aspect of their game quite well in this series. The only concern will be the form of Virat Kohli but given the class of the former captain, a big score might just be around the corner.

Hello and a warm welcome to the third and final ODI of this three-match ODI series between India and West Indies. India have already sealed the series with dominating performances in the first two ODIs and will be eyeing a whitewash here. West Indies, on the other hand, have a lot to ponder about and they will be desperate for a victory here with 10 World Cup Super League points up for grabs.
... MATCH DAY …
